practices.practice: Read the cluster connection string from an environment variable at runtime and provide a .env.example placeholder rather than committing credentials to source control.
practices.prior_belief: Read the cluster connection string only from the environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI at runtime and never commit actual credentials or the URI to source control or logs; provide a .env.example with a placeholder instead.
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Python
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB connection string environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI

practices.practice: Create and reuse a single, long-lived MongoClient per process (module/global singleton) instead of creating a client per request.
practices.prior_belief: Create a single, long-lived MongoDB client instance per process (reuse it across requests) and configure connection pooling (maxPoolSize/minPoolSize) rather than opening a new connection per request.

practices.practice: Always require TLS for connections and validate server certificates; do not disable certificate validation in production.
practices.prior_belief: Require TLS/SSL for all connections (tls=true/tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=false in the URI or driver TLS options) and validate server certificates to prevent MITM.

practices.practice: Store production credentials in a secret store (Azure Key Vault), rotate them, and restrict network access via firewall rules or Private Endpoints; prefer managed identity/Entra RBAC for production.
practices.prior_belief: Store and rotate database credentials in a secrets manager (e.g., Azure Key Vault) rather than in environment variables or files when possible; restrict database network access via firewall rules or VNet service endpoints.

practices.practice: Set retryWrites=false in the Azure DocumentDB connection string and verify driver-level support and implications for write retries before enabling driver-managed retryable writes.

Implement retries for transient errors with exponential backoff and jitter, honor Retry-After on 429 responses, and limit retries; combine driver retry facilities with application-level bounded retries only when operations are idempotent or deduplicated.
practices.source_name: Reliability and Throttling guidance for Azure
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB 429 throttling Retry-After exponential backoff

practices.practice: Tune connection-pool parameters according to hosting context (small pools and init outside handler for serverless; larger pools and pre-warmed minPoolSize for long-running OLTP servers).
Create indexes on fields used in filters and sorts (customer_id, action_type, channel, timestamp) and prefer well-ordered compound indexes that match common query prefixes.
practices.prior_belief: Create indexes on all fields used in filters and sorts for core queries (e.g., customer_id, action_type, channel, timestamp) and avoid collection scans for propensity and channel lookups.

practices.practice: Use explain('executionStats') / query plans to validate that queries are using indexes and to diagnose COLLSCAN or in-memory sorts.
practices.prior_belief: Use explain() / query plans to validate that your core queries are using indexes; if sorts are necessary, create compound indexes that match the sort order (e.g., {customer_id:1, timestamp:-1}).

practices.practice: For vector search, create a cosmosSearch vector index (vector-diskann / vector-hnsw / vector-ivf) with dimensions and similarity that exactly match stored embeddings, and tune index parameters (maxDegree, lBuild and query-time lSearch) for the recall/latency tradeoff.
practices.prior_belief: For vector search, create a vector index (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF as provided by the cluster) on the embedding field, store embeddings as a consistent vector type/shape, and ensure the index parameters (metric, dimension) match stored vectors.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB (vector-search)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector index DiskANN lSearch lBuild dimensions similarity

practices.practice: Normalize embeddings when using cosine similarity and store embedding metadata (model name, dimensions) alongside vectors so index/query parameters remain consistent.
Split very large vectors or low-compressibility binary fields into a side collection keyed by document id rather than embedding them in frequently-updated core documents.
practices.prior_belief: Keep embedding vectors and large binary fields in a dedicated collection (or dedicated field with careful size limits) rather than embedding large vectors in frequently-updated core customer documents to reduce document size and update cost.

practices.practice: Use TTL indexes (expireAfterSeconds) for ephemeral documents to let the service automatically remove old demo or temporary records.
practices.prior_belief: Use TTL indexes for ephemeral data (e.g., demo NBA recommendations or temporary logs) to automatically expire old documents and avoid manual cleanup.

practices.practice: Use upsert operations for idempotent writes (upsert:true) when writing recommendations to avoid duplicates and include created_at/updated_at and provenance metadata.
practices.prior_belief: Use upsert operations (findOneAndUpdate with upsert:true or updateOne with upsert) for writing recommendations to avoid duplicate documents and include created_at/updated_at and agent provenance metadata in the document.
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB upsert example updateOne upsert

practices.practice: Project only required fields in queries (use projection) when evaluating models or agents to reduce bandwidth and latency.
practices.prior_belief: Use projection to fetch only required fields (e.g., history timestamps and action types or embeddings) when evaluating propensity/channel/timing agents to reduce bandwidth and latency.

practices.practice: Page result sets using limit and a stable sort key (e.g., timestamp desc + _id) or keyset pagination rather than relying on skip for large offsets to avoid scanning skipped documents.
practices.source_name: General Azure/MongoDB pagination guidance (avoid skip; use keyset/pagination)
practices.how_found: pagination skip performance avoid skip keyset pagination

practices.practice: Enable diagnostic settings and slow-query logs and alert on CPU/memory/IOPS/storage/connection saturation; surface slow queries to guide indexing changes.
Choose storage and compute appropriately: prefer Premium SSD v2 for new clusters (IOPS gated by compute tier), and size compute for throughput not disk size.

Shard only when necessary and pick a shard key that evenly distributes load (high-cardinality for write-heavy; query-localizing key for read-heavy) and ensure queries include the shard/partition key when possible.
practices.prior_belief: Choose a partition/ shard key that evenly distributes load (e.g., customer_id) and ensure queries include the partition key when possible to take advantage of partition routing and avoid hot partitions.

practices.practice: Avoid large multi-document cross-shard transactions when possible; if transactions are required, keep them short and prefer single-partition transactions.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid large multi-document transactions when possible; if transactions are required, keep them short and, where supported, limit them to a single partition key to reduce cross-partition coordination cost.

practices.practice: When programmatically creating vector or advanced indexes, verify the cluster tier supports the requested index type (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF) and include fallback instructions or IaC that records index parameters.
practices.prior_belief: When creating indexes programmatically, verify that the cluster supports the requested index type (e.g., cosmosSearch/vector-diskann) and fall back to documented manual/CLI steps or include clear instructions in README if programmatic creation fails.

practices.practice: For local development, use the DocumentDB Gateway container and configure TLS relaxation only for local dev (tlsAllowInvalidCertificates) driven by env vars; never default to disabling cert validation in code.
Use idempotent seed scripts for demo/test data and confine test writes to the sample database (e.g., sample_customer_360_03) with the ability to run seeds repeatedly without duplication.
practices.prior_belief: When seeding test/demo data, write only to the specified database sample_customer_360_03 and to namespaced collections (e.g., sample_customer_360_03.nba_recommendations or test_ prefixes) and ensure seed scripts can be run idempotently and cleaned up.

practices.practice: Instrument and monitor KPIs (latency, QPS, 4xx/5xx, 429s) and capture slow queries and metrics to guide index additions and capacity changes.
practices.prior_belief: Instrument and log key performance indicators (latency, QPS, 4xx/5xx, 429s) and correlate them with deployment changes; capture and monitor slow queries to guide index additions and schema adjustments.

practices.practice: Persist vector index parameters (dimensions, similarity, maxDegree, lBuild) in infrastructure-as-code so index builds can be reproduced and reconstructed when embedding models change.

notes:
I inspected the sample app files (db client singleton, seed script, agents, orchestrator) and then loaded relevant installed skills and Microsoft Learn pages. Most prior beliefs about connection handling, TLS, singleton client, retries/backoff, indexing, vector-index parameter matching, upserts, projection, explain(), sharding, monitoring, and Key Vault are confirmed by DocumentDB public docs or the installed domain skills. Two prior-belief style practices (application-level audit-storage of agent inputs and explicit advice about sanitizing raw pipeline inputs) did not appear as Azure DocumentDB-specific recommendations in the official docs/skills as explicit single-line rules and were left to be handled as application-level guidance (they remain in the prior-belief list and are discussed below).
